title: Cloudflare Workers Pricing 2026: Free vs Paid Plans
summary: Cloudflare Workers pricing runs free until you hit usage limits, then costs $5 per month. Choose your tier based on expected traffic and project size.
body_markdown:
## What Cloudflare Workers costs at realistic monthly usage


From 1 million to 200 million requests a month, the bill is the $5 base plus whichever of request overage or CPU overage your workload trips first. CPU usually trips first.


> Two Workers with identical traffic can therefore bill very differently.


Take the current published rates from Cloudflare's pricing page and run the arithmetic below with your own measured CPU time.


As of November 3, 2026, Paid includes **10 million requests and 30 million CPU milliseconds** a month. Beyond that, requests cost $0.30 per additional million and CPU time costs $0.02 per additional million milliseconds.


At every volume the formula is the same:


1. Requests over the included allowance, multiplied by the per-request overage rate.
2. Total CPU milliseconds (requests × average CPU ms) over the included allowance, multiplied by the per-CPU-ms rate.
3. Add both to the $5 base.


The examples below assume an average of 10 ms of CPU per request.


### Low traffic: why Free usually holds


If traffic is steady at 1 million requests a month, Free usually holds, because the daily request cap is a daily limit and not a monthly pool. The catch is spikes.


### 10 million requests: what the $5 plan covers


At 10 million requests a month, Free is usually out because the daily cap is the constraint, and the $5 plan is where you land. Whether you pay anything beyond the base depends on average CPU time per request.


At 10 ms, 10 million requests use 100 million CPU milliseconds. The requests are fully covered, but CPU is 70 million over the allowance, which adds $1.40 and makes the month $6.40.


If a route only routes, redirects or reads a header, it often stays inside the included allowances. One that parses large JSON bodies or renders HTML may not.


### 50 and 200 million requests: overage maths


By 50 million and 200 million requests, overage becomes a real line item. Calculate request overage and CPU overage separately, then add them.


At 50 million requests, 40 million are over the allowance, which adds $12.00. CPU is 500 million ms, 470 million over, adding $9.40, so the month is $26.40.


At 200 million requests, request overage is $57.00 and CPU (2,000 million ms) adds $39.40, for $101.40 in total.


At 200 million requests, a small change in CPU per request moves the total more than the request count does.


### Why CPU time per request moves the bill most


You can forecast request overage from analytics, because it grows in a straight line with traffic. CPU overage depends on code: a routine that costs a few extra milliseconds per call is multiplied by every request you serve.


Measure real CPU time on production-like requests before you quote.
